thought.text: Network works. Installing Node.js 20 LTS via NodeSource (Ubuntu 22.04's native node is too old for webpack 5.110).

reasoning_content:
The network is available. Going to install Node.js 20 LTS using the NodeSource setup script (non-interactive). Alternatively, since it's simpler, I could also consider using the `node` package from the Ubuntu 22.04 repository, but that would be Node 12, which is too old. I'll go with NodeSource.

NodeSource setup: `curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash -` followed by `apt-get install -y nodejs`. This will add the repository and install nodejs along with npm. This is a global install, and it's a system-level operation, so the security risk is MEDIUM (it's a well-known registry, and it's necessary for the task).

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x -o /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh && bash /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh 2>&1 | tail -5; echo \"SETUP_EXIT:$?\"", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Add NodeSource Node 20 repo"}
